description:
SUMMARY: The Village entered into an agreement with Epicurean Park, LLC on September 6, 2022, for Village-wide mowing and landscape maintenance services. The agreement was subsequently amended to adjust service rates and include additional Village properties.
Epicurean Park, LLC has requested an approximately 3.7% Consumer Price Index (CPI) adjustment based on the South Florida CPI for the 12-month period ending August 2026. Additionally, the Village is requesting that five new locations be added to the existing scope of services.
The proposed Third Amendment increases the annual contract amount from $165,234.00 to $179,265.00, representing an annual increase of $14,031.00. Of this amount, $7,860.00 is attributable to the additional locations, with the remaining $6,171.00 attributable to the proposed adjustment to existing service rates.
title: Third Amendment to Epicurean Park LLC for Village Wide Landscape Maintenance Services Agreement: Approve the Third Amendment to the Agreement for Landscaping Services with Epicurean Park, LLC, revising the rates for existing services and adding five service locations for a total annual contract amount of $179,265, and authorize the Mayor to execute the amendment.

description:
SUMMARY: The HVAC system at Village Hall consists of two 50-ton units serving the first and second floors and one 10-ton unit serving the Parks and Recreation wing.
Following inspections by Trane-certified technicians, staff determined that both 50-ton condensing units were operating at approximately 50% capacity and were at risk of failure. The second-floor unit was replaced during the previous fiscal year through an emergency purchase.
Replacement of the remaining 50-ton unit serving the first floor was included in the Fiscal Year 2027 budget. Due to the unit's age and deteriorating condition, replacement is necessary to maintain reliable heating and cooling throughout Village Hall and prevent potential service interruptions. The existing 10-ton unit serving the Parks and Recreation wing remains operational and does not require replacement at this time.
Staff obtained a proposal from Hall Mechanical and Air Conditioning, LLC through the Sourcewell cooperative purchasing contract for replacement of the first-floor 50-ton condensing unit. The proposed contract amount is $107,730.16, inclusive of labor, materials, equipment, and warranty.
title: Procurement for HVAC Replacement at Village Hall: Motion to approve the construction contract with Hall Mechanical and Air Conditioning, LLC, under Sourcewell Contract No. FL-R6-HVAC-092524-HML, in the amount of $107,730.16 for replacement of the first-floor 50-ton condensing unit at Village Hall, and authorize the Mayor to execute the contract.

description:
SUMMARY: The Village is in the process of improving the South Village (SoVi) District along 2nd Avenue North from Congress Avenue to Davis Road, and Davis Road from Lake Worth Road to 2nd Avenue North. As part of these ongoing improvements, the Village recently completed Phase 1, which consisted of the stormwater system, roadway milling and resurfacing, and an 8' wide pathway on the north side of 2nd Avenue North.
The Village applied for and was awarded a FDOT Transportation Alternatives grant through the Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) in the amount of $1,288,000.00 for the completion of the Phase 2 Complete Streets Improvements along 2nd Avenue North. These improvements consist of a 10' wide multi-use path along the south side of 2nd Avenue North, landscaping with irrigation, on-street parking, signage, striping, crosswalks, and decorative stamped asphalt. Grant funds will be available in FY29 for construction, and the project must be designed and engineered in FY27.
Staff recommends that Keshavarz and Associates, Inc., which performed the design phase services for the Phase 1 stormwater project and has extensive knowledge and information on hand, complete the design phase of this project. The Village received a proposal from Keshavarz in the amount of $312,905.76, and staff is recommending approval of the Task Order for the design and engineering services.
title: Task Order No. 01 with Keshavarz and Associates for the design phase services for the 2nd Avenue North Complete Streets Project: Approve Task Order No. 01 with Keshavarz & Associates, Inc., under the June 13, 2024, Professional Services Agreement, for design, permitting, and bid-phase services for the 2nd Avenue North Complete Streets Project, Phase 2, in a total amount not to exceed $312,905.76, funded from account 001-400-410-56300.

description:
SUMMARY: The Public Works Department maintains all Village public property and rights-of-way. Each year, the Department resurfaces roads as part of this ongoing maintenance responsibility to keep the pavement safe and in good condition. After analyzing our recent pavement condition study, staff identified the roadway segments that require milling and resurfacing.
In accordance with Section 58-7 of the Purchasing Code, Alternative Purchasing Methods, the Village's Public Works Department received council approval to utilize the Palm Beach County Contract for Annual Milling and Resurfacing (Project 2024-050) via piggyback with Ranger Construction Industries to perform the work for the Village. If authorized, this agenda item will approve Work Order No. 01 for FY27 milling and resurfacing.
Roadway segments scheduled for milling and resurfacing during FY 2027 include Pinehurst Road from Davis Road to Gulfstream Road, East Lake from Shady Lane to Gulfstream Road, Shady Lane from Davis Road to Gulfstream Road, Bayside Road from Shady Lane to Gulfstream Road, the 184 Springdale Circle utility trench patch, and the Davis Road and Pinehurst Road intersection utility trench patch. The total cost of the work is $200,887.77 and will be issued under Work Order No. 01.
title: Approval of Work Order No. 01 with Ranger Construction for Milling and Paving Work: Motion to approve Work Order No. 01 for the milling and paving work as budgeted in FY27. The Village will utilize the previously approved piggyback agreement with Ranger Construction Industries through the Palm Beach County Engineering and Public Works Agreement Contract No. 2024050 - Milling and Resurfacing Continuing Services Construction. Funding is available from Account Number 01441-55300.

SUMMARY: Staff recommends that the Village Council approve the use of the City of Deerfield Beach’s cooperative award under ITB No. 25-017 for as-needed purchases of water meter fittings, water line accessories, and fire hydrant accessories. These materials support the operation and maintenance of the Village’s utility systems.
Under Section 58-7 of the Village Purchasing Code, staff proposes using the Southeast Florida Governmental Purchasing Cooperative Group award to purchase from two of the three awarded vendors: Ferguson US Holdings, Inc. d/b/a Ferguson Enterprises, LLC, and Fortiline, Inc. d/b/a Fortiline Waterworks. The Deerfield Beach City Commission approved the award on June 3, 2025, following a competitive solicitation. Both vendors currently supply the Village and have provided reliable service and quality products.
If approved, the Village would purchase eligible products at the awarded discount off current manufacturer list prices, subject to the applicable contract terms. The underlying contracts provide for up to two additional one-year renewals, subject to the applicable renewal provisions. Purchases will be funded through the Water & Sewer Enterprise Fund and limited to the amounts appropriated for each fiscal year.
The Village Attorney prepared the proposed agreement and reviewed it with the Utilities Director, Assistant Utilities Director, and Finance Director.

description:
SUMMARY: The Utilities Department, throughout the year, has a need to purchase quicklime, which is a critical chemical component in the water treatment process that enables organic contaminants to be saturated and attach to sand that is used in the process; thus, providing a higher quality of water for our customers.
The Village currently obtains Quicklime through a cooperative purchasing agreement from the Southeast Florida Government Purchasing Cooperative (Co-Op) — Furnish, Deliver and Discharge Quicklime (Contract #23-36B). The City of Tamarac renewed the contract for an additional three (3) year term from November 1, 2026, through October 31, 2029.
In accordance with Section 58-7 of the Purchasing Code, Alternative Purchasing Methods, staff recommends continuing to utilize the Southeast Florida Government Purchasing Cooperative contract and Lhoist North America of Alabama, LLC for Quicklime. Under the proposed agreement, the Village will receive the previous year's price plus Consumer Price Index (CPI-U) plus 1% for each consecutive contract year. The agreement will expire on October 31, 2029.
The Village Attorney prepared and reviewed the proposed agreement in coordination with Utilities and Finance staff. The Village has previously worked with Lhoist North America of Alabama, LLC and reports satisfactory service and product quality.
title: Furnish, Deliver and Discharge Quicklime — Cooperative Purchasing Contract Renewal — Utilities Department (FY 2027 Budget Funded - Water & Sewer Enterprise Fund): Motion to approve the Cooperative Purchasing contract renewal with Lhoist North America of Alabama, LLC for the purchase of Quicklime, utilizing the Southeast Florida Government Purchasing Cooperative Contract No. Contract 23-36B, furnish, Deliver and Discharge Quicklime, for the period ending October 31, 2029, in an amount not to exceed the funds appropriated in the FY 2027 Water & Sewer Enterprise Fund.

SUMMARY: The Utilities Department throughout the year has a need to employ the services of a vendor to assist in the repair of motors and pumps throughout the Village's wastewater collection system (i.e. lift station pumps to pump sewage) and two (2) water treatment plants (i.e. high service pumps to deliver drinking water to our customers).
In accordance with Section 58-7 of the Purchasing Code, Alternative Purchasing Methods, staff is recommending the Village use the renewed Martin County contract awarded to Tripp Electric Motors. Martin County completed a competitive selection process for Motor & Pump Repair (RFB# 2023-3545). The contract was renewed by Martin County on September 30, 2026.
If approved, the Village would accept MCE Tripp Electric Motors, LLC's pricing utilizing the Martin County contract, including all terms, conditions, and pricing therein. The term of the proposed agreement would expire on November 6, 2027, and may be renewed for one (1) additional one (1) year period. The Village will not expend more than the amount in the approved budget, as it may be adopted/amended annually for these goods and services over the contract term.
The Village Attorney prepared and reviewed the proposed Agreement with the Utilities Director, Assistant Utilities Director, and Finance Director. The Village has worked with the proposed vendor and has received excellent service and quality products.

description:
SUMMARY: The Police Department is requesting Village Council approval for the purchase of forty-five (45) Dell Pro Rugged Laptops and four (4) Dell Pro Docks at a total cost of $143,306.36, utilizing NASPO Contract No. C000001116132.
The police department relies on laptop computers to support daily law enforcement operations, report writing, investigations, administrative functions, and access to essential department systems.
The department’s existing laptops are either out of warranty or have warranties scheduled to expire between FY27 and FY29. As technology continues to advance, aging equipment becomes less efficient and may experience reduced performance, reliability concerns, and compatibility challenges with updated software and operating systems.
The proposed purchase will initiate a phased replacement plan, replacing the entire fleet of laptops utilized by officers in the field, as well as laptops for three (3) workstations in the office environment. The remaining laptop replacements are anticipated to be completed in FY28. This approach will allow the department to prioritize operational needs while maintaining a structured equipment replacement schedule.
Replacing the existing laptops will improve operational efficiency, reduce equipment downtime, and ensure continued compatibility with essential law enforcement applications and security requirements.
The Dell Pro Rugged Laptops are specifically designed to withstand demanding conditions associated with law enforcement operations while providing the performance and durability necessary for daily use. The additional docking stations will support designated workstations, allowing personnel to transition efficiently between mobile and desktop working environments.
Staff recommends that the Village Council approve the purchase of forty-five (45) Dell Pro Rugged Laptops and four (4) Dell Pro Docks, utilizing NASPO Contract No. C000001116132, in an amount not to exceed $143,306.36.
The Village’s Purchasing Code, Section 58-7 – Alternative Purchasing Methods, provides that the Village may utilize an alternative purchasing method for any purchase in lieu of obtaining competing price quotations or quotes or issuing a competitive purchase solicitation if the criteria set forth in the Procurement Policy for each alternative purchasing method is satisfied.
title: Purchase of Replacement Laptops for Police Department Personnel - Police Department (FY 2027 Budget Funded) - NASPO Master Agreement No. 23026: Authorize the purchase of forty-five (45) Dell Pro Rugged laptops and four (4) docking stations from Dell Marketing L.P., utilizing NASPO Master Agreement No. 23026 and Florida Alternate Contract Source Agreement No. 43210000-23-NASPO-ACS, in an amount not to exceed $143,306.36

description:
SUMMARY: The Police Department requests authorization to expend up to $14,000 in Police Forfeiture Funds to purchase and install Wi-Fi equipment in the Police Department Community Room.
The Community Room has never had Wi-Fi access. The proposed installation will establish a new capability to support law enforcement training, police-sponsored community programs, and public safety events. The Village's Information Technology (IT) Department evaluated and selected the equipment. The system will provide guest internet access independent of the Village's internal networks, allowing instructors and training participants to access online training materials and resources without compromising Village network security.
The current quoted equipment cost is $9,658.05; however, a recent price increase is anticipated. The Police Department requests authorization of up to $14,000 to accommodate potential price increases and ensure project completion. The Police Department's Forfeiture Fund account has sufficient funds.
The proposed equipment purchase qualifies as a "small purchase" under Section 58-4(a) of the Village Code. To ensure competitive pricing, the IT staff conducted market research in accordance with Sections 5.1(A) and (B) of the Village's Procurement Policy.
Additionally, the proposed expenditure is consistent with Florida Statutes, Section 932.7055(5)(a), which authorizes the use of forfeiture funds for law enforcement purposes, including the purchase of additional equipment. This expenditure will establish a new technological capability that enhances the Department's training resources and supports its community policing and public safety initiatives.
title: Authorize Police Forfeiture Fund Expenditure for Wi-Fi Equipment in the Police Department Community Room: Move to authorize the expenditure of an amount not to exceed $14,000 from the Village’s Special Law Enforcement Trust Fund to purchase and install Wi-Fi equipment in the Police Department Community Room to support law enforcement training and police-sponsored community programs

description:
SUMMARY: Stephen Cohen from Land Maker, Inc., agent for DTNK 1, LLC, the property owner of the abutting commercial property located at 2918 2nd Avenue North, is requesting the abandonment of a 10'-wide platted alley dedicated to the public via the Belle Vue Park plat (Plat Book 13, Page 67). The platted alley bisects the property into two parcels and results in underutilization of commercial property since the alley cannot be encumbered.
The 10' wide alley is 135' long with an area of 1,355 square feet. The applicant's property abuts the alley on both sides; therefore, upon abandonment of the public interest, interest or title will transfer solely to the applicant.
Note: The alley on the east side of Belle View was abandoned on January 8, 2015, under Resolution No. 2015-01.
The applicant has provided written confirmation from utility companies that there are no facilities within the alley, and they do not object to the abandonment.
Staff finds that the alley does not serve a public benefit, and abandonment of the alley will allow the abutting parcel to be unified as a viable development parcel.
The Planning & Zoning Board considered this item during its regular meeting on October 13, 2026, and recommended approval.
If approved, the applicant will be required to replant the area, according to the approved site plan.

description:
SUMMARY: Thomas Chmielewski, from Insite Studio and agent for the owner, Janus PS LLC, is requesting a Major Site Development Plan (SPR26-08) with two (2) waivers to allow the development of the site with the construction of a total of 120,000 square feet warehouse building, including a 100,000 square foot warehouse space and a 20,000 square foot showroom and office space.
Note: The vacant 7.38-acre property is currently undeveloped, and proposed access to the site will be via a full-access driveway connection on Lake Worth Road.
The proposed warehouse/showroom use will accommodate the relocation of the existing Padron Flooring business, which currently operates in the Village as well as Lake Worth Beach, thereby maintaining continuity of operations within the surrounding area. The proposed development will support the continued growth of Padron’s flooring business, contribute to local economic activity, and provide additional employment opportunities.
The site will provide standard parking spaces to accommodate both showroom visitors and employees during hours of operation. Drive aisles have been designed and widened to accommodate approximately 65-foot semi-trucks, which will circulate to the rear of the building where loading bays are provided for loading and unloading operations.
Additionally, the site plan incorporates a wetland preservation area and a stormwater retention lake, both located toward the rear of the property adjacent to the Lake Worth L-12 Drainage Canal. These features are designed to provide effective stormwater management, enhance environmental protection, and create a natural buffer between the proposed development and the canal.
The building is designed to emulate an office/showroom appearance, incorporating architectural elements along the Lake Worth Road façade that contribute to the streetscape. Primary bay doors are oriented away from adjacent streets, including Lake Worth Road, and are adequately screened from nearby commercial properties to the east.
As part of the proposed Major Site Development Plan, they are requesting two (2) waivers:
Waiver #1: Relief from Section 34-1329(5)(p) — to allow a reduction of parking spaces from the 150 spaces required to 89 spaces, a reduction of 61 parking spaces.
Waiver #2: Relief from Section 34-161(c)(a) — to not provide a tree within two terminal parking islands that are located under a canopy on the south side of the building.
The Planning & Zoning Board considered this item during its regular meeting on October 13, 2026, and recommended approval.
The Planning, Zoning, and Building Staff does not object to the applicant's request and recommends conditional approval to facilitate the development project proposed for the property.

description:
SUMMARY: The subject property, proposed for annexation, is generally located east of South Congress Avenue, west of South Florida Mango Road, and north of Forest Hill Boulevard.
On behalf of the Contract Purchaser, FL Residential Solution, LLC ("Applicant"), Urban Design Studio has requested the voluntary annexation of the property into the Village of Palm Springs in accordance with Section 171.044, Florida Statutes.
The 3.81-acre property is currently being developed with a 3,050 sf place of worship building, and the applicants intend to redevelop the property with a 48-unit fee-simple townhouse residential community. The Village will assign a proposed village land use and zoning designation under a separate ordinance following the annexation process.
The Village Staff finds the annexation complies with Chapter 171, Florida Statutes, because the proposed annexation is compact and contiguous to the Village boundaries under statutory annexation criteria. The subject property is located within the Village's adopted future annexation area and is within the Palm Beach County utility service area. Additionally, the property is located adjacent to the Congress Avenue District of the Palm Springs CRA.
Palm Beach County issued a letter on June 26, 2026, stating that it has no concerns about the annexation and that the proposed annexation is consistent with Florida Statutes and the policies in the County's Comprehensive Plan.
The proposed ordinance was approved by the Village Council on first reading during the October 8, 2026, meeting and is being presented for consideration for the 2nd and final reading.

description:
SUMMARY: An application submitted by Urban Design Studio on behalf of the Contract Purchaser, FL Residential Solution, LLC (“Applicant”), for a Planned Unit Development Site Plan (SPR26-09) with two waivers, for the construction of 48-unit residential townhomes on one (1) parcel located at 1580 Prairie Road totaling 3.81 acres and generally located between Forest Hill Boulevard and Cherokee Road on the east side of Prairie Road.
Note: The original application included a request for a waiver to reduce the width of the interior setbacks from 20' to 15' for the north and south property lines to allow for a 26-foot-wide interior driveway and 5-foot-wide sidewalks on both sides. At the Planning & Zoning Board meeting on September 8, 2026, surrounding residents were opposed to the reduction of the setbacks. The applicant voluntarily commits to revising the site plan, mitigating some neighbors’ concerns. The Site Plan has been amended to comply with the 20-foot side interior setbacks by reducing the private internal driveway to 20 feet in width with a 6-foot-wide sidewalk on one side.
The applicant is the contract purchaser of the subject property and is requesting approval of the Planned Unit Development Site Plan to develop the ±3.81-acre Residential Multiple-Family property, which is currently a religious place. The subject property is proposed to be redeveloped with a planned residential development comprised of 48 fee-simple townhome structures. Each unit supports a one-car garage with two additional parking spaces in the driveway, 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, a living room, and a kitchen. The community will have one access driveway via the existing Prairie Road right-of-way. Amenities include: a picnic area with grills, a pavilion, a playground, a dog park with dog amenities, and a leisure area with benches.

SUMMARY: At the Council Workshop held on November 4, 2026, staff presented a series of priority capital projects identified as critical to meeting the Village’s long‑term infrastructure and facility needs. Council provided consensus direction to pursue funding for these projects through the issuance of a General Obligation (G.O.) Bond.
The proposed G.O. Bond (or series of bonds), up to an amount of $35 million, would fund the projects reviewed during the November 4 Joint Workshop. If the referendum is approved by the voters, staff would issue a competitive Request for Proposal (RFP) for a direct‑purchase bank term loan. Based on current market conditions and loan structures, staff is projecting annual debt service of approximately $2 million per year, depending on the final term, to be supported through a dedicated debt service millage.
Approval of the attached resolution will allow the Village’s financial advisor and bond counsel to prepare ballot language, statutory notices, schedules, and other required materials necessary to place the G.O. Bond referendum on the March 2027 ballot.

SUMMARY: The purpose of this Joint Board Workshop is to discuss the proposed $35 million General Obligation Bond Referendum for potential parks, parkland acquisition, and neighborhood roadway safety improvements. The workshop will provide an opportunity for Board members to review proposed projects, funding considerations, and potential ballot language for the March 9, 2027, Municipal Election, and provide feedback and recommendations.
The proposed General Obligation Bond Referendum, if approved by voters, would authorize the issuance of bonds in an amount not to exceed $35 million. Debt service would be funded through ad valorem property taxes. The estimated financial impact on property owners will depend on the final bond structure, interest rates, and repayment terms.

description:
SUMMARY: The Utilities Department recommends approval of contracts with TCLM Enterprise, Inc., Industry Standard, and Hinterland Group, LLC to provide water utility maintenance and repair services on an emergency and non-emergency basis.
The services will support the Village's utility infrastructure, including water production, transmission and distribution systems; wastewater collection, transmission and reclamation systems; and reuse water transmission facilities. Work will be performed as needed through individual work authorizations in accordance with the contracts. The solicitation contemplated awarding contracts to multiple vendors.
On July 6, 2026, the Village issued a Request for Proposals for Water Utility Maintenance and Repair services. Proposals were due on August 5, 2026, at 2:00 p.m.The Village received six proposals from:Johnson-Davis Incorporated
TCLM Enterprise, Inc.
Industry Standard
Intercounty Engineering, Inc. (Incomplete)
DRMP
Hinterland Group, LLC
A four-member evaluation committee appointed by the Village Manager, consisting of representatives from the Utilities, Public Works, and Planning, Zoning & Building Departments, met on August 24, 2026, to evaluate the proposals. The proposals were evaluated based on the proposer's ability to respond, resources and similar project experience, pricing and overall cost to the Village, and references/experience. Based on the committee's collective scoring, the committee unanimously recommended awarding it to the three highest-ranked firms:TCLM Enterprise, Inc.
Industry Standard
Hinterland Group, LLC
The Village posted its Notice of Intent to Award on August 26, 2026.

attachments.name: First Amendment to Piggyback - Allied Universal

description:
SUMMARY: The Utilities Department uses sodium hypochlorite as an essential chemical in the Village's water treatment process. Sodium hypochlorite works in conjunction with ammonia to produce chloramine, which the Village uses as a long-lasting disinfectant to support regulatory compliance and the delivery of high-quality drinking water to its customers.
The Village currently obtains sodium hypochlorite through a piggyback of Charlotte County's competitively solicited Water and Wastewater Chemicals – Annual Contract (Contract No. 20250605). Charlotte County renewed the contract for an additional one-year term from October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2027.
Staff recommends continuing to utilize the Charlotte County contract and Allied Universal Corporation for sodium hypochlorite. Under the proposed agreement, the Village will receive the same contract pricing of $1.77 per gallon, with no increase from the previous price. The agreement will expire September 30, 2027.
Section 58-9 of the Village Purchasing Code permits the Village to access or "piggyback" contracts awarded by other governmental entities when the same or substantially similar goods or services were competitively solicited.
The Village Attorney prepared and reviewed the proposed agreement in coordination with Utilities and Finance staff. The Village has previously worked with Allied Universal Corporation and reports satisfactory service and product quality.
title: Sodium Hypochlorite Contract - Piggyback Renewal - Utilities Department (FY 2027 Budget Funded - Water & Sewer Enterprise Fund): Motion to approve the Piggyback Agreement with Allied Universal Corporation for the purchase and delivery of sodium hypochlorite at $1.77 per gallon, utilizing Charlotte County Contract No. 20250605, Water and Wastewater Chemicals – Annual Contract, for the period ending September 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed the funds appropriated in the FY 2027 Water & Sewer Enterprise Fund.

Notice of Public Hearing - 1580 Prairie Road

description:
SUMMARY: The subject property, proposed for annexation, is generally located east of South Congress Avenue, west of South Florida Mango Road, and north of Forest Hill Boulevard.
On behalf of the Contract Purchaser, FL Residential Solution, LLC ("Applicant"), Urban Design Studio has requested the voluntary annexation of the property into the Village of Palm Springs in accordance with Section 171.044, Florida Statutes.
The 3.81-acre property is currently being developed with a 3,050 sf place of worship building, and the applicants intend to redevelop the property with a 48-unit fee-simple townhouse residential community. The Village will assign a proposed village land use and zoning designation under a separate ordinance following the annexation process.
The Village Staff finds the annexation complies with Chapter 171, Florida Statutes, because the proposed annexation is compact and contiguous to the Village boundaries under statutory annexation criteria. The subject property is located within the Village's adopted future annexation area and is within the Palm Beach County utility service area. Additionally, the property is located adjacent to the Congress Avenue District of the Palm Springs CRA.
Palm Beach County issued a letter on June 26, 2026, stating that it has no concerns about the annexation and that the proposed annexation is consistent with Florida Statutes and the policies in the County's Comprehensive Plan.
The Village Council is considering the proposed ordinance on First Reading, and if approved, proposed Ordinance No. 2026-07 will be presented at the November 19th meeting .
title: (First Reading) Ordinance No. 2026-07 - Voluntary Annexation — 1580 Prairie Road: Motion to approve the application submitted by Urban Design Studio, acting as agent for the applicants and contract purchaser, FL Residential Solution, LLC. The applicants are requesting the voluntary annexation of the property at 1580 Prairie Road into the Village of Palm Springs, pursuant to Section 171.044, Florida Statutes.

attachments.name: Ordinance No. 2026-06 - Establish Millage Rate FY 26-27

description:
SUMMARY: The Village Council is requested to establish the final operating and debt service millage (property tax) rates for the Village of Palm Springs for the upcoming Fiscal Year (FY 26–27) beginning October 1, 2026, and ending September 30, 2027. Additionally, the Council is requested to consider certifying the Village's taxable value to the PBC Property Appraiser as well as other related financial information:
The Village received Form DR-420 — Certification of Taxable Value and Form DR-420 Debt — Certification of Voted Debt Millage from the PBC Property Appraiser's Office. These forms certify the Village's taxable values for the upcoming fiscal year (FY 26/27) as well as other related financial
information:The gross taxable value of all properties within the Village for the fiscal year (FY 26/27) was $2,450,202,215, an increase of $164,060,835 over the fiscal year (FY 25/26).
The rolled-back rate is calculated at 3.7319 per 1,000 taxable values. The Village's fiscal year (FY 26/27) operating millage for the General Fund is $3.50 per $1,000 of the taxable value, or a decrease of 6.21% below the rolled-back rate (At 100% collection, the expected operating millage is expected to generate $8,575,707.75. In ad-valorem tax revenue, however, the Village budgets at approximately 95% collection ratio; thus, the proposed budgeted revenue is expected to be $8,074,507.The total taxable value within the Village to calculate the debt service millage rate is $2,454,565,746; thus, the proposed millage rate required to pay the Village's general obligation debt for the fiscal year (FY 26/27) is $0.1746 per $1,000 of taxable value. That is a decrease of 0.0176 from the fiscal year (FY 26/27).
The combined millage rates for the fiscal year (FY 26/27) (3.5000 operating + 0.1746 debt = 3.6746 total mills) is .0176 mills lower than the combined approved millage rates for the fiscal year (FY 25/26) (3.5000 operating + 0.1922 debt = 3.6922 total mills).
The gross taxable increment value (TIF) for the Palm Springs Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) for the fiscal year (FY 26/27) is $276,141,879. The Palm Springs CRA will receive TIF funding from the Village of Palm Springs and Palm Beach County at the Village's approved millage rate - a proposed $3.50 per $1,000 taxable value. At 100% collection, the total increment/revenue expected to generate is $959,725. However, the Village budgets at a 95% collection ratio; thus,
The proposed budgeted increment/revenue expected is ($911,739). This is the seventh year the Village has had the Palm Springs CRA.
Ordinance No. 2026-06 establishes the millage rates for the fiscal year (FY 26/27). If approved on the first reading, the proposed fiscal year (FY 26/27) millage rate ordinance will be presented to the Village Council for consideration at the second and final reading on Thursday, September 24, 2026, Council meeting.
Note: Following first reading, Ordinance No. 2026-06 will be publicly noticed as required by State Statutes. The staff will submit the required Form DR-420 - Certification of Taxable Value and the Form DR 420 Debt — Certification of Voted Debt Millage to the PBC Property Appraiser, PBC Tax Collector, and the State of Florida.
title: (First Reading/First Public Hearing) Ordinance No. 2026-06 — Establish Fiscal Year (FY 26/27) Millage Rates - Operating & Debt Service: Motion to approve Ordinance No. 2026-06 on First Reading for the FY 26-27 operating millage rate for the Village of Palm Springs is hereby levied for 3.5000 mills which is a 6.21% decrease, below the rolled-back rate of $3.7319. The real property tax roll for the current calendar year has been certified by the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser for a nonexempt valuation of $2,350,086,404 and of tangible personal property for nonexempt valuation of $100,115,811 of a total gross taxable value for operating purposes of $2,450,202,215. If approved, the final public hearing to adopt the FY 26-27 millage rate for operating and debt service is scheduled for September 24, 2026.

description:
SUMMARY: Mr. Mark Brenchley, agent for Walmart ("Applicant and Tenant"), is requesting a sign variance approval (PSV26-19) from Section 34-328(a)(1), Wall Signs, to allow a 42.46 square foot sign above the pharmacy drive-thru window on the west side of the building facing an interior drive aisle.
Note: in July 2015, the Village Council approved a site plan amendment with special exception to add a drive-thru window to the proposed Walmart Neighborhood Market/Pharmacy, with a waiver for two queuing spaces instead of the required five spaces. At that time, a wall sign was not proposed for this new service.
Wall signs are regulated by Section 34-328 of the Village Land Development Regulations, which specifies that the maximum permitted area for a wall sign shall be determined by a formula using the square footage of the building’s face fronting a public street right-of-way. The proposed sign will face an interior drive aisle in lieu of a public right-of-way.
Staff has reviewed the application and determined that the proposed variance would not create conflicts with surrounding businesses. If this side of the building faces the right of way, a 75 square foot sign will be permitted to be installed.
Staff does support the applicant’s request and recommends conditional approval.
title: (Quasi-Judicial Hearing) Resolution No.2026-32: Wall Sign Variance (PSV26-19) — Walmart Neighborhood Market — Pharmacy Drive-Through - 4316 Forest Hill Boulevard, Unit 4400: Consideration of a sign variance request (PSV26-19) by Mr. Mark Brenchley, agent for Walmart, seeking approval, with conditions, to allow a 42.46 square footwall sign above the pharmacy drive-thru window on the west side of the building, facing an interior drive aisle, in deviation from Section 34-328(a)(1) of the Village Land Development Regulations.

Staff recommends that the Village Council approve the amended CDBG Capital Improvement Agreement and authorize the appropriate officials to execute the revised agreement.

description:
SUMMARY: An Ordinance of the Village of Palm Springs amending Article VI, Division 7, Chapter 34 of the Village of Palm Springs, entitled General Employees' Pension Plan, amending Section 34-892 to provide for pension contributions by DROP members; deferred retirement option plan to provide for a five (5) year DROP; providing for codification, conflict, severability, and an effective date.
The General Pension Plan Ordinance needs to be amended to reflect negotiated changes to the pension plan regarding the addition of a five (5) year DROP participation period.
DROP accounts earn interest compounded monthly at an effective annual rate of 4%.
Retirement benefits paid into DROP are also increased by the 3% annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) each October 1st.
Upon termination of employment, the proceeds of the DROP account will be distributed in one of three ways:By a lump-sum payment;
By direct rollover, or
By a combined partial lump-sum payment and rollover.

SUMMARY: KMG Holdings LLC (property and business owner) is requesting approval of a permit to paint a (1) mural sign to paint the art of the company’s official logo, a stylized and abstract floral design composed of four petal-like shapes in red, yellow, teal and light blue on the east of the building located at 2925 10th Avenue North, which is visible from the public right-of-way.
Note: the business "Haven Health Management," located on the property, is an administrative office building that borders 10th Avenue North and Summer Street.
Currently, the property is developed as a 28,092 square foot commercial structure located on the northwest corner of 10th Avenue North and Summer Street. The applicant proposes a mural on the east facade facing Summer Street right-of-way.
The proposed mural is displayed on the central facade of the building, featuring the company's official logo, a stylized and abstract floral design that will serve as a visual representation of the organization's identity and values.The east elevation of the building: 529.49 square feet is proposed, which represents 9% of the building's east facade.
The Village's Code, Section 34-295 Mural permits; purpose; application; review; issuance; fees; provides that the Village Council will review a mural permit application based on the following:The mural will enhance the aesthetic beauty of the area and is compatible (in terms of size, location, design, etc.) with the structure on which it will be displayed as well as the surrounding neighborhood.
The mural has balance, order, symmetry, and harmony in the design.
The material will not require excessive maintenance by its owner.
There are no more than two (2) murals on the premises, and the size of each is not greater than 550 square feet.
There are no other murals within 1,000 feet of the proposed art forms.
The proposed mural is located within a commercial zone district.
Note: The proposed mural was painted by Cody Parker with an exterior UV clear coat and lifetime warranty hold. This premium quality and protective, durable finish resists fading, cracking, peeling, and the formation of mildew on the surface. Regular maintenance is key.
The Staff recommends approval of the proposed murals. However, due to the sun and the humid conditions that we consistently experience in southeastern Florida, the Planning, Zoning, and Building Department staff recommends that all mural permits be conditioned as follows:
The mural(s) shall be maintained in good condition.
Graffiti, denaturation, cracking, color change, and/or fading, as determined by the Police Chief and/or the Planning, Zoning & Building Director, shall require immediate restoration or removal of the artwork within 30 days of written notice from the Village.
Note: If approved, the Village would have the authority to rescind the mural permit and require the applicant to either maintain and/or remove the murals through code enforcement proceedings, if they are not maintained in accordance with the proposed mural permit.

description:
SUMMARY: As required by the annual review of the fund balance policy, staff recommends consideration and approval of an updated resolution amending Resolution No. 2025‑11, originally adopted on July 10, 2025, to reflect the Village's Fund Balance Policy.
Resolution No. 2025‑11 was adopted to formalize the Village’s Fund Balance Policy; however, the resolution language did not fully align with the policy as written. The policy was designed to establish a reserve of 25–30% of the General Fund’s annual operations and maintenance budget, excluding depreciation, amortization, capital expenditures, and interest expenses.
The resolution adopted on July 10, 2025, inadvertently applied the 25–30% reserve target to the entire General Fund budget, including capital costs, which was not the policy's intent and does not reflect the Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA) Best Practices.
The updated resolution corrects this discrepancy by reaffirming that the reserve target applies only to the operations and maintenance portion of the General Fund budget.
In addition, the original policy established a $3 million Emergency Reserve for emergency declarations, natural disasters, or other unforeseen critical events. The updated resolution retains this requirement in full.
Staff recommends that the City Council approve the updated resolution amending Resolution No. 2025‑11 to reflect the original intent of the Fund Balance Policy, including:Applying the 25–30% reserve target to the General Fund’s operations and maintenance budget only, excluding depreciation, amortization, capital, and interest expenses.
Maintaining the $3 million Emergency Reserve for disaster or emergency response.
title: Proposed Resolution No. 2026-20 Update Fund Balance Policy to Reflect Policy Change: Approve an amendment to Resolution No. 2025‑11 to align the Village’s Fund Balance Policy with GFOA Best Practices by applying the 25–30% reserve target to General Fund Operations and maintenance only and maintaining the $3 million emergency reserve.

SUMMARY: The HVAC system at Village Hall is comprised of 2ea 50-ton units and 1ea 10-ton unit which cool and heat the entire facility. Staff recently had all of the units inspected by Trane certified technicians and determined that the 50 ton condensing unit that runs the second floor of Village Hall is operating at 50% capacity and at risk of catastrophic failure. Given the age of the 50 ton condensing unit, procuring parts to repair the system is becoming increasingly more difficult and costly. In order to maintain the facility in full operability, replacement of the 50tn unit is a necessity and must be performed as soon as possible.
Staff procured a proposal through the Sourcewell Cooperative Purchase contracted vendor, Hall Mechanical and Air Conditioning LLC, for the replacement of the 50ton condensing unit to replace the existing failing condensing unit. The proposal is at a cost not to exceed $107,730.16 which is inclusive of all labor, material, equipment, and warranty. Given the high level of consequence and long lead times to receive the replacement 50-ton condensing unit, staff proceeded with the emergency procurement of the unit per the Village's Procurement policy, and is now presenting the item to council for ratification.

This means that for every $1 that the Village receives from the grant, it will have to contribute $2 towards the project.
However, to be eligible for the grant, the Village must provide matching funds of $1,000,000 before July 1, 2027. This matching fund can be included in the Village's capital improvement plan, which is a long-term plan to fund infrastructure and other capital projects.
The proposed performance area project is expected to bring significant benefits to the community, such as creating a space for cultural events, performances, and other outdoor activities. With this added space, the Village is able to offer programming that will help enhance the overall appeal of Village Commons Park, making it a more attractive destination for residents and other members of the public looking to become engaged in cultural activities.
The grant presents an opportunity for the Village of Palm Springs to make a significant investment in its cultural and recreational offerings. By securing the grant, the Village can make the proposed amphitheater a reality, and provide a valuable asset to the community for years to come.

description:
SUMMARY: At its April 20, 2026, meeting, the Palm Springs CRA Board authorized staff to proceed with a Request for Proposals for a redevelopment loan. A redevelopment loan, or tax increment revenue note, would provide the CRA with financial flexibility to leverage developers' investments and may support infrastructure, public realm amenities, development gap financing, and/or parcel acquisition.
The proposed Resolution No. 2026-19 authorizes the CRA to enter into a Loan Agreement with Truist Bank. The terms of the Loan Agreement provide for issuance of a Tax Increment Revenue Note in an amount not to exceed $10,000,000. The proposed resolution further approves an Interlocal Agreement between the CRA and the Village, which guarantees payment of debt service on the loan should there be insufficient funds in the CRA Trust Fund to cover the annual debt payment.
The CRA issued a competitive Request for Proposals for a direct purchase bank term loan. Two (2) responses were received from SouthState Bank and Truist Bank. After comparing the responses and consulting with the Village/CRA's financial advisor, PFM, the CRA Executive Director and Village Finance Director recommend that the CRA accept Truist Bank's offer. Truist Bank offered a fixed, taxable interest rate of 5.37% that would be locked through an anticipated closing date no later than July 26, 2026. This rate provides the CRA with optional prepayment flexibility starting with a 5% premium that declines to a par call (no penalty) on the 10th anniversary of the closing date.
Annual debt service will be paid over a fifteen (15) year term starting in August 2027 in the amount of $989,375 for both CRA Districts combined. Projections indicate that available TIF revenues for debt service will grow substantially in the coming years.

The warehouse areas will not be open to the public and will be for the exclusive use of the businesses on the property.

The applicants are not proposing any exterior changes to the existing buildings A, B, or C, nor any increase in the overall square footage of the buildings. All existing architectural features and site improvements will remain in their current constructed state.
The scope of the amendment is limited to interior modifications within Building B to accommodate an increase of forty (40) additional beds within existing bedroom spaces. These changes are confined to the building’s interior and do not impact the overall footprint, massing, or external appearance of the structure. There is no distinction among the client population to be treated, only by their primary diagnosis.
The purpose of the requested amendment is to meet the ongoing increasing demand within the primary mental health space since the COVID pandemic. No addiction treatment services are expected to be provided on the property. However, persons with co-occurring disorders of both Substance Use Disorder and Mental Health may be treated onsite on a case-by-case basis.
The hours of operation for this facility are 24/7; staff are on-site 24 hours a day, with clinicians present during the day working 8-hour shifts. The staff-to-resident ratio for clinicians is 1:10, and overall staff during waking hours is 1:15. The overall need for staff has been evaluated, and it has been determined that 50 staff members on the greatest shift is sufficient for the increase in beds.
The Planning & Zoning Board considered this application during their May 12, 2026, meeting and recommended approval.
The Planning, Zoning & Building Staff does not object to the proposed amendments and recommends conditional approval.

description:
SUMMARY: The Utility department is requesting the approval of amendment No.1 to the existing Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) Agreement for the Utilities Operations Building Project to establish the Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) pursuant to Section 7.2 of the Agreement and authorize the transition from pre-construction services into the construction phase of the project.
On January 15, 2026, the Village Council approved the Construction Manager at Risk Agreement for the Utilities Operations Building Project – Kaufman Lynn Construction Inc., for the pre-construction services of the Utilities Operations Building (TO No. 331).
The pre-construction phase included coordination with the Architect, Engineer, and Project Management teams for constructibility reviews, project scheduling, cost estimating, value engineering evaluations, and development of the Guaranteed Maximum Price proposal.
The CMAR has completed the pre-construction phase and associated services for the design development and preparation of the GMP proposal as outlined in Section 7.1 of the Agreement.
Section 7.2 of the Agreement provides that, upon acceptance of the GMP by the Village Council, the Contract shall be amended to establish the final GMP amount for construction services and authorize monthly payments associated with the Cost of the Work and Construction Manager’s Fee as outlined in the Agreement.
This amendment to the existing CMAR Agreement will:
Establish the final Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for the Utilities Operations Building Project in the amount of $13,573,062.00
Authorize the Construction Manager at Risk – Kaufman Lynn Construction Inc. to proceed with the construction phase of the project pursuant to Section 7.2 of the Agreement.
Incorporate the finalized GMP proposal, construction schedule, allowances, contingencies, Direct Owner Purchase (DOP) procedures for applicable tax savings, and associated contract documents into the Agreement.
Establish a construction duration of 12-14 months.
The Contract for Construction Manager at Risk Services with Kaufman Lynn Construction, Inc. provides for a direct purchase program in which the Village will purchase certain construction materials included in the GMP for the Utilities Operations Building to utilize our tax-exempt status and receive sales tax savings (savings currently estimated at $103,517.00, 1% of the building's construction cost). The Contract includes a direct purchase process in which Kaufman Lynn will vet (through a competitive process) and recommend vendors to the Village. These construction materials include, but are not limited to the generator and switchgear, fuel system components, doors and windows, concrete, and structural steel components. If accepted, the Village will issue a Purchase Order to the vendor to acquire the item or materials.
Staff is seeking Council authorization to waive the standard purchasing process for acquisitions necessary for the Utilities Operations Building construction effort as best interest acquisitions. The individual expenses are expected to be over $50,000.00, which is the threshold for council approval set by the Purchasing Policy.
NOTE:
The GMP amount does not include certain owner-procured project-related costs, including but not limited to
furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E) – Approximately $180,000.00
Builder’s Risk insurance – Approximately $95,000.00
Owners Representative Services — Approximately $230,000
Temporary Facilities & Warehouse Storage — Approximately $87,000
Other owner-purchased items associated with the overall completion of the project.
Village Staff recommends approval of the amendment to the existing CMAR Agreement establishing the Guaranteed Maximum Price pursuant to Section 7.2 of the Agreement and authorizing the Construction Manager, Kaufman Lynn Construction Inc. to proceed with construction services for the Utilities Operations Building Project. Additionally, staff is seeking Council authorization to waive the standard purchasing process for acquisitions necessary for the Utilities Operations Building construction effort as best interest acquisitions.

description:
SUMMARY: A strategic plan serves as a roadmap for an organization. It establishes long-term direction, priorities, and measurable goals that are all used in operational decision-making and resource allocation. A strategic plan is not a business plan. It focuses on needs or gaps in service that necessitate deliberate focus in order to carry the organization towards its Vision.
Based on Village Council input on priorities (during 1-on-1 meetings in February), six (6) goal areas are proposed, which are further described in the working draft of the Strategic Plan:Celebrate Residential Neighborhoods
Facilitate Redevelopment and Economic Growth
Foster a Culture of Engagement and Participation
Efficient, Effective and Empathetic Service Delivery
Community Policing to Strengthen Community Trust
Enhance Literacy (and Improve School Grades)
The Management Team has collectively crafted Strategic Objectives for each goal or Focus Area, as well as Key Results, which measure the big picture that the Village Council will be focusing on versus day-to-day activities that individual departments might monitor and measure as Key Performance Indicators.
Staff is seeking Village Council input on the working draft so that we may finalize the strategic objectives and key results into a final document to bring back for approval.
title: Provide Direction Regarding the Village's Strategic Plan

description:
SUMMARY: An Ordinance of the Village of Palm Springs amending Article VI, Division 7, Chapter 34 of the Village of Palm Springs, entitled General Employees' Pension Plan, amending Section 34-892 to provide for pension contributions by DROP members; deferred retirement option plan to provide for a five (5) year DROP; providing for codification, conflict, severability, and an effective date.
The General Pension Plan Ordinance needs to be amended to reflect negotiated changes to the pension plan regarding the addition of a five (5)- year DROP participation period.
DROP accounts earn interest compounded monthly at an effective annual rate of 4%.
Retirement benefits paid into DROP are also increased by the 3% annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) each October 1st.
Upon termination of employment, the proceeds of the DROP account will be distributed in one of three ways:By a lump-sum payment;
By direct rollover, or
By a combined partial lump-sum payment and rollover.
If the Employee should die while in DROP, their designated beneficiary would be eligible to receive their accumulated DROP benefits.Depending on the benefit option you selected, your beneficiary may also be eligible to receive a continuing monthly benefit.
Or, if their beneficiary does not qualify for a continuing benefit, and the benefits deposited in their DROP account add up to less than any employee contributions they may have made (including amounts they may have paid to upgrade service or buy service credit), their beneficiary may receive a refund of the difference.
However, because the employee retired upon entering DROP, they are not eligible for disability benefits.
Note: Following First Reading, a minor amendment was made to clarify that elected officials were eligible for the DROP and considered employees for the purposes of this pension plan.
This change is administrative in nature and does not alter the proposed or the effective date of the ordinance.
The Village Council approved Ordinance No. 2026-01 on First Reading at the May 14, 2026, Meeting. Ordinance No. 2026-01 is being presented to Council for the Second and Final Reading and approval.

description:
SUMMARY: Ordinance No. 97-05 established the annual compensation for the Mayor and Members of the Village Council, effective March 11, 1997. The ordinance established annual compensation consisting of a salary of $4,200 for the Mayor and $3,600 for each Council Member, along with annual expense allowances of $2,400 for the Mayor and $1,800 for each Council Member.
Since 1997, these compensation levels have not been adjusted and no longer reflect the responsibilities associated with serving in elected office or the compensation provided by comparable municipalities. The proposed ordinance increases the Mayor's annual salary to $10,000 and each Council Member's annual salary to $9,400. In addition, the annual expense allowance would increase to $5,000 for the Mayor and $4,400 for each Council Member.
Note: Following First Reading, a minor amendment was made to clarify the annual adjustment of the expense allowance. The ordinance now provides that the expense allocation for the Mayor and each Council Member shall be adjusted annually based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI), utilizing data published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics for the Southern Urban Region, All Urban Consumers. Annual adjustments will be calculated using CPI data available each March and applied at the end of April beginning in 2030. No changes were made to the proposed salary amounts approved at First Reading.
This change is administrative in nature and does not alter the proposed salary amounts or the effective date of the ordinance.
The Village Council approved Ordinance No. 2026-03 on the First Reading at their May 14, 2026, meeting. Ordinance No. 2026-03 is presented to Council for the Second and Final Reading for approval.

description:
SUMMARY: Ms. Tatiana Acosta, agent for the Applicant, Squeeky's Car Wash, is requesting two (2) sign variances to install a monument sign with an electronic changeable copy on the existing car wash facility located at 3263 Lake Worth Road.
The proposed digital sign will display a variety of colors, along with the message, which is a deviation from code allowances for electronic signs. The applicant describes that the 10 square feet (10 sf) sign includes an integrated LED message board occupying no more than 25% of the total sign face area with an overall height of seven feet (7’) in compliance with the applicable setback.
The applicant is seeking two (2) sign variances:
1. PSV26-12 — A request to allow an electronically changeable monument sign (provide relief from Section 34-267 of the Village Code that limits changeable electronic signs to public service messages on governmental, public, or educational properties).
2. PSV26-13 - Request to allow multiple colors and varying messages (provide relief from Section 34-267(i) of the Village Code that limits changeable electronic signs to a monochromatic, single message)
The sign structure consists of an aluminum cabinet with acrylic faces and internal LED illumination, supported by a concrete footing designed in accordance with the Florida Building Code. The LED message board will include automatic brightness adjustment to ensure compliance with illumination standards and to minimize visual impact. The LED message board is proposed as a limited and integrated component of the monument sign and is intended solely to improve operational communication and site safety.
The sign will operate under the following conditions as a voluntary commitment from the applicant:Message will be static only.
Each message will remain displayed for a minimum of 24 hours.
Content will be limited to operational, safety, and community-related information.
No animation, flashing, scrolling text, or video-style content.
Automatic dimming control will regulate brightness based on the ambient lighting conditions.
Based on previous Village council direction, the staff is concerned with establishing precedent for allowing commercial businesses to utilize changeable electronic signs and allowing graphics on electronic signs.
If approved, the staff recommends that Council approval should be contingent on the sign complying with the limitations of Section 34-267, which prohibit animation or video displays and require that sign messages remain static for a minimum of six seconds, with an instantaneous change in display occurring within one second or less, and the five conditions listed in the Staff Report.

description:
SUMMARY: Schmidt Nichols, agent for John Lewis, MGR, 1591 Kirk Road Partners LLC (“Applicant”), is requesting approval of a Special Exception Use Amendment (PSSE26-03) and concurrently requesting a waiver to allow the restaurant with the bar to operate as an ancillary use within the previously approved Court Club, which operates as a privately owned membership club, within the residential multifamily property located at 1591 Kirk Road.
The property received site plan approval on March 18, 2025, to develop a 17,683 square foot recreational facility consisting of a tennis-racquet club with 14 courts for tennis, pickleball, paddleball, and approximately 10,000 square feet of a clubhouse building.
The Applicant seeks to amend the previously approved Special Exception Use to clarify that the facility will operate as a privately-owned membership club, with a restaurant and a bar as ancillary components to the principal recreational use.
As part of the proposed amendment, the applicant is requesting a waiver to allow alcohol sales within 500' of a public school. Section 34-830, Distance between Establishments that Sell Alcoholic Beverages, applies to properties within the CG zoning district. Business operations, including restaurants that serve alcohol, are typically not allowed in the RM zoning district. The applicant is approved for a private Racquet club, a permissible use within the RM district, with an accessory clubhouse and restaurant. In the spirit of the intent of the Code, staff is processing a waiver on the distance separation requirement that would typically be required for a commercial operation for the sale of alcohol within the clubhouse and restaurant.
The requested waiver is limited solely to the ancillary food and beverage component and does not alter the approved recreational use or its overall operational intensity. The proposed clarification and associated waiver are consistent with the intent of the original approval and do not introduce any new or more intensive use of the property.
This application does not propose any modifications to the previously approved site plan. Rather, the request is limited to clarifying the operational characteristics of the approved use and addressing code requirements necessary to facilitate a liquor license.
The Planning & Zoning Board considered this application during their May 12, 2026, meeting and recommended approval.
Planning, Zoning, and Building staff do not object to the applicant's request and recommend conditional approval.

description:
SUMMARY: The Utilities Department must replace sixteen (16) aging wastewater pumps at lift stations throughout the Village's utility service area with submersible pumps. Failures and inefficiencies were observed with the pumps, which had to be replaced. It's anticipated that the Village will save money by upgrading the pumps to newer, more reliable, and more efficient submersible pumps, thereby reducing electricity use and staff maintenance costs. Our utility customers will benefit from improved operational efficiency.
Note: To ensure the lowest possible price and to standardize the types of pumps, accessories, and repair services utilized within our utility processes, the Village issued an Invitation to Bid (ITB) and awarded contracts to three (3) qualified vendors — PSI Technologies, Inc. SUMMARY: The Utilities Department recommends retaining an Owner’s Representative to serve as project manager for the Utilities Operations Building Project (Task Order No. 331). The Owner’s Representative will protect the Village’s interests and coordinate with the Construction Manager at Risk (Kaufman Lynn) and Design Professionals (Currie Sowers Aguila Architects and CHA Consulting, Inc.). The current Owner’s Representative, Greg Siefker, has announced his retirement. To ensure project continuity, Village staff recommended Kaziah Construction Management, LLC, with Matt Kaziah as the new Owner’s Representative. Matt Kaziah has over 20 years of construction management experience, including leading projects such as the South Florida Water Management District Environmental Services Laboratory, Zimmer Biomet Medical Device Manufacturing Facility, and the Trauma Hawk Helicopter Hangar at Palm Beach International Airport. His experience will provide technical oversight, coordination, and project control beyond what Village staff can provide. The scope of services provided as the Village's Owner's Representative includes:
Pre-Construction Services:Assist in completing the design with the Engineer/Architect and CMAR.
Look for value engineering opportunities.
Provide professional review of contract documents with supporting vendors.
Review of permit and scope documents to support pricing.
Review of the Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) Proposal from the CM at risk.
Construction Services:Participate in telephone and electronic communications with the client and project team to coordinate the project, discuss Project strategy, and provide periodic updates.
OAC meetings are anticipated weekly, with separate update meetings scheduled as needed for utilities management.
Review proposed contract changes in order to validate changes or scope deficiencies and confirm that proposed material and labor rates are in line.
Review the validation of Contractors' monthly pay applications and vendors' invoices. Manage all Notices to Owner and log monthly partial releases associated with the contractor's applications for payment.
Coordinate with the Village of Palm Springs Building Department staff to develop a punch list of items needed to obtain a certificate of completion for each project component.
Support the warranty process and compilation of manufacturers' warranties.
Support Project closeout with a review of final lien releases and Final Affidavit by the General Contractor.
Kaziah Construction Management, LLC will provide services at an hourly rate of $215. The estimated average is 15–20 hours during pre-construction and 15–20 hours per week during construction, depending on the phase. The total consulting fee will not exceed $292,400, which is about 1.5% of the anticipated project budget, below the industry range of 3–10% for similar project management services. Note: Greg Siefker, the current Owner’s Representative, has recommended Kaziah Construction Management, LLC. Village staff support this recommendation. Kaziah Construction Management, LLC has agreed to the Professional Services Agreement prepared by the Village Attorney.

description:
SUMMARY: The Palm Springs Police Department requests Council approval for a new supervisory position, Community Policing/Traffic Sergeant. This role will directly oversee the Community Policing and Traffic Units, which include five officers and a Community Service Aid. Establishing this position will improve supervision, increase effectiveness, and support the Village’s priorities.
Unit Workload and Operational Demands
The Traffic Unit has expanded its mission to include traffic-homicide investigations, requiring extensive coordination and specialized training. The Community Policing Unit manages special events and community outreach, advancing long-term engagement goals. The Training Sergeant has, among other duties, the critical responsibility for firearms qualifications, asset management, and FDLE Officer certification.
Justification for Establishing the Position
Creating a dedicated Community Policing and Traffic Sergeant will improve oversight, accountability, coordination, and deployment. It will expand community-engagement initiatives, enhance traffic enforcement strategies, and create balanced supervisory spans of control. The new Sergeant will be tasked with providing innovative training to road patrol using best practices to foster meaningful, daily engagement with the public in a non-enforcement capacity. Moreover, this position will be instrumental in integrating the department’s Road Patrol operations into a true Community Policing & Neighborhood-Centric form of policing, shifting our culture to meet the desires of the community.
Importance of Maintaining a Dedicated Training Sergeant
Training responsibilities—including firearms instruction, weapons maintenance, certification tracking, and compliance—are essential to the Department's professionalism and readiness. A dedicated Training Sergeant ensures quality, reduces liability, and supports officer development.
Conclusion and Recommendation
Staff recommend approval of the Community Policing / Traffic Sergeant position. This role will strengthen supervisory capacity, expand community-policing efforts, improve traffic safety operations, and align with the Village's strategic public-safety objectives.
title: Request for a New Community Policing Sergeant Position — Police Department: Consider approval for the addition of one sworn supervisory position, the Community Policing/Traffic Sergeant, within the Palm Springs Police Department. This position will provide dedicated supervision for the Community Policing and Traffic Units, enhancing operational effectiveness and supporting Village public safety objectives.

SUMMARY: An Ordinance of the Village of Palm Springs amending Article VI, Division 7, Chapter 34 of the Village of Palm Springs, entitled General Employees' Pension Plan, amending Section 34-892 to provide for pension contributions by DROP members; deferred retirement option plan to provide for a five (5) year DROP; providing for codification, conflict, severability, and an effective date.
The General Pension Plan Ordinance needs to be amended to reflect negotiated changes to the pension plan regarding the addition of a five (5)- year DROP participation period.
DROP accounts earn interest compounded monthly at an effective annual rate of 4%.
Retirement benefits paid into DROP are also increased by the 3% annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) each October 1st.
Upon termination of employment, the proceeds of the DROP account will be distributed in one of three ways:By a lump-sum payment;
By direct rollover, or
By a combined partial lump-sum payment and rollover.
If the Employee should die while in DROP, their designated beneficiary would be eligible to receive their accumulated DROP benefits.Depending on the benefit option you selected, your beneficiary may also be eligible to receive a continuing monthly benefit.
Or, if their beneficiary does not qualify for a continuing benefit, and the benefits deposited in their DROP account add up to less than any employee contributions they may have made (including amounts they may have paid to upgrade service or buy service credit), their beneficiary may receive a refund of the difference.
However, because the employee retired upon entering DROP, they are not eligible for disability benefits.

description:
SUMMARY: Ordinance 97-05 established the Annual Compensation for the Mayor and the Members of the Village Council, which became effective March 11, 1997. It established the total compensation of the Mayor including "salary" of $4,200 per year for the Mayor and $3,600 per year for the Council Members, plus "expenses" of $2,400 per year for the Mayor, and $1,800.00 per year for each Council Member deemed "annual salary. Since 1997, the rates of the Council have not been adjusted and are no longer competitive with the market of other municipalities. They also do not take into account the increased level of responsibility in their roles.
The recommendation for compensation is to increase the Mayor's salary to $10,000 per year and the Council member to $9,400 per year, along with increasing annual "expenses" to the Mayor of $5,000 per year and $4,400 per year to each Council member.
Section 3.04 of the Village Charter states that the Council may determine the annual salary of the council members and mayor by ordinance, but no ordinance increasing such salary shall become effective until all terms of those currently in office have expired. Effective March 2027, Council Member District 2 and District 4 end. Effective March 2028, Council Member District 3 and District 4 and Mayor's terms end. This ordinance will become effective after the end of those terms in April 2028.

description:
SUMMARY: The Public Works Department is actively engaged in the repair, maintenance and construction of sidewalks throughout the Village. The Village recently completed Vision Zero Action Plan and Mobility Plan studies that are intended to enhance safety improvements for all users of our roadway network, in particular pedestrians and bicyclists. One of the corridors that was identified for pedestrian and bicycle safety was Alemeda Drive from the park connector pathway to Davis Road. This corridor currently has an 8' wide sidewalk on the south side that was constructed recently adjacent to the athletic park facility. The opposite side of the roadway has 5' wide sidewalks that are in poor condition and are scheduled to be replaced with new 8' wide sidewalks as part of this project.
The Village advertised the project to the Pre-qualified Public Works Minor Construction Contractors on February 12, 2026, and received a total of 5 proposals from all 5 pre-qualified vendors. On February 27, 2026, the Village opened the bid proposals and the lowest, most responsive and responsible contractor was RMJ Contractors. Staff is recommending approval of Task Order No. 05 to RMJ Contractors for the construction of the Alemeda Drive Sidewalk Replacement Project at a cost not to exceed $195,650. The original approved FY26 budget of $150,000 for this project was insufficient due to the continued increase in material and labor costs within the heavy construction market. The increased costs will be funded from unspent funds within the Capital account.

description:
SUMMARY: The Utilities Department is making an emergency repair to the automatic transfer switch (ATS) at the R.L. Pratt Water Treatment Plant. An ATS is a device that automatically switches the electrical load from the primary power source to the backup generator during a power outage, ensuring a continuous power supply. The current ATS has failed, and the plant currently requires a manual switch of electrical load. With the upcoming hurricane season approaching, and a 30-week lead time from the ATS manufacturer, the staff recommends approving the repair as an emergency purchase.
The cost of the replacement ATS is $98,750.00 and includes the equipment, installation, all necessary restoration, and the supply of a temporary power generator for use during the ATS installation. The Utilities Department's contingency account will be used to support the emergency repair.
The proposed vendor has been a subcontractor for other Village projects, and the Village has received excellent service.​

description:
SUMMARY: The Police Department had previously requested and received Council approval to use Police Forfeiture Funds to purchase crime scene forensic equipment for the newly constructed crime lab. Four of the Five items requested are in the process of being purchased with the approved Forfeiture funds. For the last requested item, the Alternate Light Source, the department had to seek a different brand due to the original brand being discontinued from production. After due diligence, the lowest cost from a vendor for the newly selected Alternate Light Source is approximately $13,000 over the initially approved funding level. The Department is requesting the approval of the additional funding from the Police Forfeiture Fund account.
The purchase of this crime scene forensic equipment goes beyond the normal operating expenses of the police department. The above equipment is widely used in crime labs to assist in processing evidence. The Alternate Light Source is used to detect invisible trace evidence such as touch DNA or blood which is a critical component in solving crimes.
The item above falls under the definition of a “small purchase” Sec. 58-4(a) in the Village Code. To ensure the lowest possible prices, the Police Department staff has done market research the above item in accordance with the Village Procurement Policy Section 5.1 A&B.
The approximate cost for the equipment Alternate Light Source $34,000 (an additional $13,000 over the previously approved cost) and is available in the Police Department’s Forfeiture Account.
This expenditure also complies with Florida State Statute 932.7055 (5a) that specifically states, in part, that these funds shall be used for “law enforcement purposes, which include… providing additional equipment.”
title: Use of Police Forfeiture Funds: Request for approval of additional funding from the Police Forfeiture Fund in the amount of approximately $13,000 to complete the purchase of an Alternate Light Source for the crime lab, due to a change in vendor and increased cost, in compliance with Village procurement policy and Florida Statute 932.7055.
